While you ride, the app keeps searching from the next stop you can reach. It only reports a real alternative – get off earlier, change elsewhere, take another line – that you can still reach with your own vehicle\'s current live time. “From %1$d′”: at your transfer level, at least %1$d minutes sooner (Settings › Notifications). “Every minute”: sprint changes included, from 1 minute sooner.
Only ways that arrive at least this much sooner. With “Every minute counts” from 1 minute.

These changes leave less time by the live times than the walk needs even at a brisk pace. You only make them by running or if the departing ride leaves late. Use them at your own risk.

For this trip only: the transfer level jumps to Sprint and the shortcut alert switches on. The app keeps searching from the next stop you can reach, tight and sprint changes included, and alerts you with sound from 1 minute faster. It never switches by itself: you decide.
With \"Every minute counts\" on, a followed trip is offered a made-up way 1 to 3 minutes faster, marked \"Simulation\", through the same card and notification. For testing only.

Every leg stands where its times say. Separate: short legs get smaller blocks, without the change minutes, their name or at last as a thin bar. Combine: a run of short legs is one block with the colours and names of their lines.

While you follow a trip, the app keeps searching in the background – with your usual transfer times – and shows a quiet notification when something changed since you chose it and a real alternative is at least as much faster as set below (3 minutes by default). One tap takes it over; it never switches by itself.
Only ways with no more changes than yours and none tighter than your transfer times.
In the first 3 minutes of a trip only alert for ways at least 3 minutes faster.
Two helpers on the way. The shortcut alert looks for something faster in the background on every trip you follow. “Every minute counts” you switch on for one trip only.
computed from realtime data, not GPS
Vehicle positions are estimated from the timetable and realtime messages, not measured by GPS. A green dot on a vehicle means current realtime data; without a dot, it runs by the timetable.
A small note at the bottom of the map: vehicles are placed from realtime data, not GPS.
Only when zoomed in close – saves data and battery.
Automatic: entrances close up, lifts closer, escalators closest or at the marked station. Always: all of them from close up. Selected only: only those of the station you picked.

Where the way is known from map data: the real walk at your pace plus %1$s for getting off and finding the way, at least %2$d′.
Between a platform and a stop in the street: the walk plus %1$s for getting off and the stairs.
Where no way is known, rules of thumb: %1$d′ on the same platform, %2$d′ to another platform, %3$d′ at large stations with regional or long-distance trains, a walk of the provider plus %4$d′.
The levels: time to spare beyond that
less, but it works at a brisk pace (the walk in %1$d %% of the time, no buffer) and the change is at least %2$d′
otherwise: only by running or with luck
Where the live arrival is only estimated (the provider\'s forecast does not fit), a change is normal at best, and tight with less than %1$d′ to spare.
Only the change itself counts, not which search found the journey: the same change has the same live times and the same level in every journey.
